newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to pay off former guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to pay off former guerrillas.

text.p: South Africa's defence ministry sought parliamentary approval on Tuesday for a scheme to pay off former liberation fighters who choose not to join the integrated post-apartheid army.

Deputy defence minister Ronnie Kasrils, who could benefit from the scheme himself, said the government estimated that about 6,000 of the 40,000 registered guerrilla veterans would prefer the gratuity to a military career.
Gratuities range from 12,000 rand ($2,560) to 42,000 rand, but Kasrils said that at an average payoff of 30,000 rand, the scheme would cost a total of about 210 million rand.

Guerrillas who fought apartheid from bases in neighbouring countries for almost 30 years are entitled to a position in a new, integrated South African National Defence Force, but some are too old or ill and many say they don't want to be soldiers in a peacetime army.

"We are dealing with the recognition of services to the liberation of our country," said Kasrils, who was a commander in the military wing of President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress (ANC).
He said ANC guerrillas fought apartheid without pay, without a pension scheme and without provision for their integration into the society they helped to free from white rule.
"The minister of defence is looking at quite an intense human issue -- people that have basically not a cent in their pockets," he said.
Officials said the Demobilisation Bill would be debated in parliament on Friday and was unlikely to face opposition.
